analysis.investment_thesis: GB Logistics looks statistically cheap at P/E 2.64 with strong ROE of 26.4% and ROCE of 28.2%, but at just INR 29.5 Cr market cap, incorporated only in 2019, and with a vague "full truckload + trading" story, this is a micro-cap lottery ticket, not a Lynch-style compounder. Without a visible growth rate, PEG cannot even be computed — and in logistics, a sub-3 P/E usually signals the market doesn't trust the earnings.
key_strengths: Rock-bottom P/E of 2.64 — if earnings are real, huge re-rating potential
Promoter holding at 52.4% shows founder skin in the game
key_risks: INR 29.5 Cr nano-cap — illiquid, prone to manipulation, no institutional cover (FII 0.29%)
Trucking + trading is a low-moat, fragmented, commoditized business
Only 6 years old (incorporated 2019) with no multi-year earnings track record to trust
red_flags: P/E of 2.64 in a cyclical trucking business often means earnings are peak/unsustainable
'Trading of products' mixed with freight — opaque revenue mix
Near-zero institutional ownership suggests no serious diligence has been done
analysis.detailed_analysis:
From a Lynch lens, I need a story I can explain in a minute: "GB Logistics runs trucks and trades stuff." That's not a story, that's a description. I love cheap stocks — P/E 2.64 with 26% ROE is the kind of line that makes me pick up the phone — but in Indian micro-caps at INR 29.5 Cr, a sub-3 P/E almost always reflects earnings the market expects to evaporate. Full truckload freight is brutally competitive, diesel-sensitive, and commoditized; the "trading" sleeve is a black box that often inflates reported revenue with razor-thin margins.

Without a disclosed earnings growth rate, I cannot compute a PEG — the single most important number in my toolkit. The good news: 52.4% promoter stake means alignment, and the returns on capital are genuinely excellent if sustainable. The bad news: 0.29% FII and 2.18% DII means no serious analyst has validated the books, and a 2019-incorporated company has no cycle-tested track record. This could be a 5-bagger if the numbers are clean and growth is 25%+, or a zero if they're not. For my fund, I'd need to see 3 years of audited growth, customer concentration disclosure, and a plausible niche before buying. Pass until the story gets clearer.
